terms.meaning: one continuous conversation, identified by an ID.
a long random ID that is practically unique.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup for the chat store
sections.what: Brings in the store library, the API client, a random-value helper and the unique-ID generator.
sections.why: Likely reason: the random-value helper must load before the ID generator to work on the phone.
sections.watch_out: Moving the random-value import below the ID generator can cause a failure on the phone.

sections.name: ChatMessage
sections.title: Shape of one chat message
sections.what: Describes one message: an ID, who wrote it (user or assistant), the text, optional suggestions and sources, and the time.
sections.why: Gives every message the same shape.
sections.watch_out: Sources are typed loosely, so their contents are not checked.

sections.name: ChatState
sections.title: What the chat holds
sections.what: Lists the session ID, messages, loading flag, suggested questions, and the actions to send a message, start a new session or load history.
sections.why: Keeps the whole chat state in one place.
sections.watch_out: Messages are kept in memory only, so they are lost when the app restarts.

sections.name: useChatStore (part 1)
sections.title: Starting, loading and sending
sections.what: Starts with a new session and three suggested questions. Starting a new session or loading history replaces the current chat. Sending adds the user's message at once, waits for the answer, then adds it along with new suggestions.
sections.why: Likely reason: showing the message first makes the chat feel fast.
sections.watch_out: If sending fails, the user's message stays on screen and is followed by an apology.

sections.name: useChatStore (part 2)
sections.title: Failure apology
sections.what: When sending fails, adds a fixed apology from the assistant and logs the error. This is the only error the user sees.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the chat from looking stuck.
sections.watch_out: The apology is fixed English text and gives no reason, so the user cannot tell what went wrong.

summary: Holds the AI chat: the messages, the current session, suggested questions and the send action.
purpose: Lets the user ask the AI questions and read the answers.
why: Likely reason: showing the user's message first keeps the chat responsive.
how: Starts a new random session with three suggested questions. Sending a message shows it right away, waits for the answer, then adds the answer and new suggestions. If sending fails, a fixed apology is added. Loading history replaces the chat with saved messages.
inputs: The typed text, the session ID, and saved history from the server.
outputs: The messages list, the suggestions, and an apology message on failure.
risks: The failure message gives no reason. Nothing here saves the chat, so it is lost on restart unless history is loaded. The session ID is not checked before use.
debug: If the apology appears, check the log for 'Chat failed' and the server logs. If history is empty, check the session ID passed to fetchHistory.
